answer: Sunk-Cost Attestation Ledger. Each identity must anchor a unique physical artifact — a notarized river sediment sample logged with chain-of-custody at a registered wharf — whose hash is committed on-ledger. Registration requires an in-person visit where an agent forge-stamps the sample casing under camera, binding biometrics to the artifact hash. Duplicate biometrics or replayed artifact hashes are rejected at commit. An attacker pays a distinct human visit, travel, notarization, and stamping per identity — roughly $400 and four hours each, non-recoverable.
